title: Re-Dividing, Splitting or Re-Amortizing: PracticePay Patient Financing Reset Methods
content:
**Rule.** The reset payment method of a PracticePay Patient Financing plan follows the plan's promotion and ledger: a no-interest plan is re-divided, its interest-free part being the whole reset balance and its payments the reset payments; an interest-bearing plan that carries a deferred-interest billing entry is set to a split payment, its interest-free part being the reset's deferred-interest part, which is the deferred interest billed on the plan but never more than the reset balance and bears no further interest, and its payments being the due dates after the deferred-interest billing date through the final due date; any other plan is re-amortized, with no interest-free part, over the reset payments.

| Plan | Method | Interest-free part | Payments |
|---|---|---|---|
| no-interest plan | re-divided | the whole reset balance | the reset payments |
| interest-bearing, with a deferred-interest billing entry | split payment | the deferred interest billed, never more than the reset balance | the due dates after the billing date through the final due date |
| any other interest-bearing plan | re-amortized | none | the reset payments |

The payment under each method is the interest-free part divided equally over its payments plus the level payment that repays the rest of the reset balance at the reset rate over those payments.

## A plan set to a split payment, after the reset

- **Interest.** If the promotional payoff test fails, the whole memo — every period since the purchase date, not only the unpaid part — is billed to the balance on the day after the end date of the promotional period and the plan continues for the rest of its term with monthly interest charged from then on, at the plan APR, or, for a plan whose customer has asked for a payment reset under the reset schedule, and only for such a plan, at the reset rate from the reset onward, interest then running on the plan balance excluding fees and excluding the part of the reset's deferred-interest part not yet repaid.
- **Applying payments.** Each payment is applied to billed interest and billed deferred interest first, then fees, then the remaining plan balance, except on a plan whose customer has asked for a payment reset under the reset schedule, and only on such a plan, where the reset schedule itself allocates each payment from the reset onward: first the equal share of the reset's deferred-interest part that the reset payment carries, then interest billed since the reset, then fees, then the rest of the balance; every other plan applies its payments in the order first stated.

## Worked figures (hypothetical split payment)

Reset balance 2400.00 USD including 400.00 USD of billed deferred interest; 20 due dates after the billing date through the final due date; a reset rate taken as 12.00 for illustration (monthly rate 0.01). Interest-free part: 400.00 over 20, that is 20.00 a month. The rest, 2000.00, repaid at 0.01 a month over 20 payments: 110.8306… a month. Split payment: 20.00 plus 110.8306…, that is 130.8306…, rounded up to the next cent once, at the end: 130.84 USD.
